subject.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels

question: Should CLI reseed prompts trust both top-level sender fields and persisted `__openclaw` names/usernames as participant attribution, or restrict rendering to the canonical persisted envelope and stable identity?
rationale: The patch changes how untrusted group-participant metadata is represented to the model, and code inspection alone cannot establish the intended identity and spoofing policy.

options.title: Use Canonical Envelope
options.body: Render only maintainer-approved `__openclaw` sender metadata, treating stable sender ID as authoritative and names as presentation text.

options.title: Approve Dual Sources
options.body: Keep top-level priority plus envelope fallback and explicitly accept both locations as trusted attribution inputs for CLI history.

options.title: Pause Attribution Rendering
options.body: Defer this renderer until one shared sender-attribution contract defines source precedence and model-facing semantics across transcript consumers.

recommendation.title: Use Canonical Envelope
recommendation.body: Render only maintainer-approved `__openclaw` sender metadata, treating stable sender ID as authoritative and names as presentation text.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged canonical sender-metadata persistence contract that this renderer consumes.
